question: Should OpenClaw make `gateway.readiness`, `registerReadinessCriterion`, and the four standard hosting profiles supported public V1 contracts, including their selection precedence and fail-closed readiness semantics?
rationale: This PR is technically structured as a feature layer, but it permanently expands operator and plugin contracts and intentionally changes when a selected deployment reports ready; that acceptance cannot be inferred from tests alone.

options.title: Approve the V1 contract
options.body: Accept the public readiness and profile direction, then require a rebased profile-only PR with current-head package-installed upgrade and conformance proof.

options.title: Land core readiness without plugin registration
options.body: Keep the generic core evaluator and defer the public Plugin SDK callback and profile compositions until a narrower contract is accepted.

options.title: Defer the feature series
options.body: Retain current readiness behavior and revisit hosting profiles only after maintainer sponsorship and a settled deployment-support scope.

recommendation.title: Approve the V1 contract
recommendation.body: Accept the public readiness and profile direction, then require a rebased profile-only PR with current-head package-installed upgrade and conformance proof.

likelyOwner.reason: This contributor authored the connected readiness and hosting-profile series and is best placed to clarify the proposed contract while a maintainer makes the product decision.
